title: Javascript / Typescript
summary: End-to-end typing on both sides of the stack, with Zod at the boundaries.
description:
TypeScript is where I spend most of my time these days, and I use it on both sides of the stack: React and Next.js on the front end, Node.js and Express on the back. I'm a firm believer in typing things end to end, and in validating anything that crosses a boundary at runtime – Zod schemas for API responses, form payloads and environment config have saved me more debugging hours than I can count.

Recent examples: [Linkarium](/projects), a Next.js link-sharing app.

title: React, Next.js & Astro
summary: React by default, plus Angular and Vue on production work.
description:
React is my default, whether as a Next.js app, as Astro islands, or as a Chrome extension UI. I led the rebuild of the [appetize.io](https://appetize.io) marketing site in AstroJS, taking Lighthouse performance from ~60% to 90%+ and accessibility, best practices and SEO from ~75% to 95–100%.

I've also worked with the other two major front-end frameworks – Angular on an accounting platform, Vue on e-commerce work – so I stay comfortable picking up whichever one a team already uses.

title: Java & Spring Boot
summary: Spring Boot APIs and production platforms, since university.
description:
Java has been with me since university and through most of my career: migrating legacy systems to Spring-based APIs at Booking.com, and building a production accounting platform at Resourcify that the operations team used daily to reconcile thousands of records.

Spring Boot is my go-to for backend work, usually alongside Hibernate, Maven or Gradle, and Cucumber for behaviour-driven tests.

title: AI-assisted development
summary: LLMs as a workflow, with guardrails and verification around them.
description:
Since 2024 I have used Claude daily as a working collaborator: navigating unfamiliar codebases, scaffolding boilerplate and weighing implementation approaches, always through the same review and test discipline as any other change. At Appetize I turned that into a team workflow, with guardrails around it: local context only and no proprietary data exposure.

I also build *with* models: a [Chrome extension](/projects) that screens job ads via Gemini or a local Ollama model, and a CV pipeline where every generated line must cite a source in a Markdown evidence corpus.

title: APIs
summary: REST aggregators, GraphQL, and integrations like Stripe and enterprise SSO.
description:
I possess extensive experience developing APIs, in particular using the REST architecture. At Booking.com I maintained the Suppliers API – an aggregator service communicating with hundreds of car rental systems, sending order requests, updates and cancellations – and at Resourcify I worked on the Recycler API behind the core platform.

More recently I've done substantial work on third-party integrations: a Stripe billing setup spanning four plans with monthly and annual options, driven by webhooks, and self-serve enterprise SSO over SAML and OIDC. I've also delved into the realm of GraphQL.

title: Web & UIs
summary: Tailwind and component libraries, accessibility and Core Web Vitals.
description:
Working on the front-end is always good fun and gives me the chance to explore frameworks like Tailwind and Bootstrap, component libraries such as Radix and shadcn/ui, and UI design techniques. I care as much about the parts that don't show – accessibility, Core Web Vitals, semantic markup – as about the visual side.

I've built web apps for various uni, work and personal projects – [check them out](/projects).

title: Testing & automation
summary: Vitest, Playwright and Cucumber, plus headless browsers for the rest.
description:
Tests are the part of the job I'm least willing to negotiate on. At Appetize I expanded end-to-end coverage from 50% to 90%+ while still shipping iteratively, and I've written BDD suites with Cucumber on Java projects.

On personal projects I use Vitest for units and Playwright for end-to-end flows – the URL parser in [Linkarium](/projects) ended up with the densest coverage in the codebase for good reason. Headless browsers do double duty for me: Puppeteer renders PDF invoices in FlexInvoice, and drives scrapers for sites that fight back.

title: Python
summary: My go-to for tooling: scrapers, batch editors, an MSc dissertation.
description:
I taught myself Python and it quickly became one of my favourite languages. I first used it to build an automated assessment tool for CompSci programming assignments, the focus of my MSc dissertation.

It's still what I reach for when a job needs doing: a [toolkit](/projects) for safely batch-editing the tags of a 12,000-track music library – every mutating command dry-runs, backs up and verifies the audio fingerprint afterwards – and a configurable multi-site property scraper whose selectors live in SQLite rather than in code.

title: Databases
summary: Postgres, MySQL and MongoDB in production; SQLite for local stores.
description:
A Library Manager was the project that introduced me to complex relational DB architectures. Since then I've designed several systems for personal and work projects, mostly with Postgres and MySQL, as well as MongoDB and Firestore in the NoSQL world, and more recently Supabase for hosted Postgres with full-text search.

I'm also fond of SQLite for anything that needs a local store: caches, scraper configuration, small bots that have to survive a restart.

title: Cloud & DevOps
summary: AWS, Docker and Kubernetes, with CI/CD from Jenkins to GitHub Actions.
description:
I've worked with AWS on production platforms, containerised applications with Docker and run them on Kubernetes, and supported a platform team through the containerisation of a large e-commerce application.

On the delivery side I've used Bamboo, Jenkins and GitHub Actions for CI/CD, and I deploy my own projects to Vercel, Netlify and a home NAS – the last one being a useful reminder that not everything needs a cloud bill.

title: Mobile development
summary: Kotlin on Android and Swift on iOS; a fiscal-code app past 100,000 downloads.
description:
I started learning Kotlin a few years ago, intrigued by its features and its possibilities for mobile development. The most successful outcome so far is an Android app that computes and validates the Italian fiscal code, which has passed 100,000 downloads on the Play Store.

On the iOS side, I've followed Stanford's *CS193p - Developing Apps for iOS* course and am carrying on as an autodidact. Flutter and React Native are still on the list.

title: PHP
summary: Over a year in Drupal on a large-scale e-commerce platform.
description:
The booking management service of a previous company was written in PHP – kind of a shock therapy experience, still an excellent chance to learn about this language. At BJSS I then spent over a year in Drupal, maintaining a large-scale e-commerce platform and architecting a GDPR-compliant cookie consent system across nine production domains.

There's still much more to explore and discover, but I like challenges.

title: C#
summary: ASP.NET on a security-focused medical store, during my BSc.
description: Medicus, an online store web application designed for selling medical products, was a collaborative project I participated in during my BSc Information Security course. Built using ASP.NET, this project placed a strong emphasis on ensuring the security and privacy of our customers.
